title: Parallelism on 8x RTX PRO 5000 72GB over PCIe (dual NUMA): naive TP8 beats TP4-on-one-node and DP-attention for a dense 27B

hardware.interconnect: PCIe only, no NVLink; GPU0-3 NODE within NUMA0, GPU4-7 NODE within NUMA1, cross-group SYS
hardware.topology_summary: nvidia-smi topo -m: 4+4 GPUs split across two CPU sockets
hardware.cpu_numa: 2 x Xeon Platinum 8488C, 192 threads; GPU0-3 -> NUMA0, GPU4-7 -> NUMA1; 1.5 TB RAM

workload.server_notes: mem-fraction-static 0.85, chunked-prefill 32768, max-running-requests 64, KV cache bf16 (auto); fresh server container per launch; raw per-run outputs in data/raw-2026-10-23-zkyd/

results.config: TP8 (all 8 GPUs, all-reduce crosses the NUMA boundary)

variance.note: output throughput across independent cold starts (fresh container each time); spread under ±1.5% for every config

methodology: sglang.bench_serving, random dataset, input 4096 / output 512 tokens, range-ratio 1; C1 = 5 prompts at max-concurrency 1, C8 = 24 prompts at max-concurrency 8; fresh server container per launch; 3 launches per config
transferable: On dual-socket x86 with no NVLink (PCIe only), naive TP8 outperformed both TP4-on-one-NUMA-node and TP8+DP-attention for a 27B dense GQA model — at this model size, compute scaling beats the cross-socket all-reduce penalty
DP-attention halved single-stream throughput at C1 (37.7 vs 75.3 tok/s): at low concurrency most DP ranks sit idle while the weights stay partitioned 8 ways
TP4 on a single NUMA node kept ~89% of TP8 C1 throughput with half the hardware — a viable config when the other 4 GPUs are needed elsewhere
not_transferable: Absolute numbers (driver, framework version, quantization dependent)
MoE models: the DP-attention + EP layout that the MiniMax M3.1-Flash launch script on this same machine uses was NOT tested here — the dense-model ranking above may reverse for MoE
Models too large to fit on 4 GPUs (they cannot take the TP4 path)
NVLink-connected systems (all-reduce cost profile is entirely different)
